summary: This memo gives IESG advice arising from reviewing Path MTU Discovery for advancement. It found that some routers optionally suppress ICMP messages, which breaks the mechanism, and outlines a change to that practice. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Computers try to find the biggest package that fits through a whole path. Some routers kept quiet about packages that were too big. This paper asks routers to speak up.

questions: why do routers need to send icmp for path mtu discovery

subtitle: Routers that suppress ICMP messages silently break Path MTU Discovery, and the IESG says how to fix it.

tldr.problem: Some routers can be set not to send ICMP messages, to protect older BSD hosts, but this makes Path MTU Discovery fail in a silent, hard to diagnose way.
tldr.mechanism: Routers should keep sending ICMP Type 3 code 4 (destination unreachable, fragmentation required and DF set) even when the switch to suppress ICMP messages is on.
tldr.outcome: Path MTU Discovery works, and older BSD hosts are unaffected because they never set the DF bit.

today: RFC 1435 is an Informational memo and the unit metadata records no obsoleting or updating RFC. It does not specify an Internet standard.

sections.title: How the Problem Was Found
sections.content:
While reviewing the Path MTU Discovery protocol (RFC 1191) for Draft Standard, the IESG learned from implementors that some vendors had added to their routers the ability to disable ICMP messages generated by the router.

The reason was to protect older BSD hosts, which would drop all connections to a host if they found an ICMP message on any of the connections, even a non-fatal one.
sections.eli5: Some routers were told to stop sending warning notes, because some old computers overreacted to every note.

sections.title: Why Path MTU Discovery Breaks
sections.content: Suppressing ICMP messages protects the older BSD hosts, but it causes MTU discovery to fail in a silent, hard to diagnose way. The sender never learns that its packets are too large for some link along the path.
sections.eli5: If nobody tells you the package is too big, you keep sending packages that never arrive and you do not know why.

sections.title: The Recommended Change
sections.content:
Routers should continue to send ICMP message Type 3 code 4 (destination unreachable, don't fragment bit sent and fragmentation required) even when their "don't send ICMP messages" switch is turned on.

This lets path MTU discovery work without affecting the older BSD hosts, since those hosts never set the DF bit in their packets.
sections.eli5: The fix: even in quiet mode, a router should still send the one note that says "this package is too big". The old computers never send such packages, so they are not bothered.

references.text: Mogul, J., and S. Deering, "Path MTU Discovery", RFC 1191, November 1990.
